name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
title: Kaynes Technology India Ltd - 543664 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Kaynes missed its FY26 revenue guidance (INR4,500 cr cut to ~INR4,000 cr, delivered ~INR3,626 cr) and OCF was about INR600 cr negative, driven by metering receivables of ~INR1,365 cr; no numeric FY27 guidance given.

summary.headline: Kaynes FY26 revenue rose 33.2% to INR3,626 crore, but missed the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance, with operating cash flow of about INR600 crore negative.
summary.overview: Management attributed the revenue shortfall to West Asia-related customer deferments, supply chain delays and one large EV two-wheeler customer cutting volumes by about 90%. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was INR5,741 million (15.8% margin) and PAT INR3,639 million (10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR12,426 million (+26% YoY) and PAT of INR912 million. Cash flow weakened sharply, driven by the smart metering subsidiary (Iskraemeco) with receivables of about INR1,365 crore, while the standalone EMS business turned cash positive. Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue number and instead guided to outgrowing the market at roughly twice the market growth rate.

financial_highlights.change: PBT hit by about INR32 crore of quarterly intangible amortisation
from 83 days FY24; management also cited 64 to 54 days

segments.name: EMS (standalone/KEMPL)
segments.commentary: FY26 EMS revenue about INR2,655 crore (Q1 INR442 crore, Q2 INR683 crore, Q3 INR667 crore, Q4 INR862 crore), growing about 26-30%. Standalone EMS operating cash flow INR250 crore positive versus INR65 crore last year; EMS receivables INR399 crore at year end versus INR379 crore at start.

segments.name: Smart metering (Iskraemeco subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR971 crore (roughly 24-25% of group revenue), with receivables about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current. Installation delays in rural areas and state-government/DISCOM payment cycles are holding up collections; securitisation has discounted only about INR40 crore so far.

segments.name: OSAT
segments.commentary: Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27. Management cites revenue visibility above INR25,000 million over five years. Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister; FY27 production estimate INR250-300 crore, export-oriented.

segments.name: PCB
segments.commentary: Management sees a confirmed demand pipeline for five years with customers seeking more capacity. FY27 production estimate INR300-400 crore; first year of operation.

segments.name: Rail (Kavach)
segments.commentary: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; approvals expected in H1 FY27, with bulk orders in H2. Management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

segments.name: EV / automotive
segments.commentary: EV segment grew about 28% in FY26 despite the large two-wheeler customer falling about 90%. Company is moving from PCB supply into assemblies and products.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 revenue number; management guides to growing at about twice the market rate (market cited at 15-18% EMS growth), with quarterly updates on market versus Kaynes growth.
Standalone EMS to stay cash positive, with working capital days improving by about 8-10 days in the coming years.
Consolidated operating cash flow: management expects the INR600 crore negative to fall by 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end.
Metering receivables and installation expected to be completed within about 3 quarters; the business will move to an EMS-component-only model for new orders.
Target of NPD-led and value-added revenue at nearly 30% of total revenue over the coming years.
Smart meter FY27 revenue expected roughly flat to slightly up or down versus INR971 crore, with about 50% of volume on the old model and about 50% on the new model.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles (Iskraemeco and August Electronics, about INR320 crore) going forward, after the Q4 catch-up of about INR32 crore.
capex_capacity: OSAT Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27 (Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister).
FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore, mainly from acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics (Canada, North America EMS), with about INR320 crore capitalised.
Mysore facility crossed INR10,000 million revenue in FY26.
Metering: about 35 lakh meters on current order, plus a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension; 2-3 months needed to complete pending supply, with installation taking 1-2 quarters more.
Launched three products now in production (SOP started), and a 9-month product launch cycle versus 12-18 months previously.
Investing in NPD engineering, co-development, digital and R&D infrastructure, and predictive maintenance / Industry 4.0 at 2 plants.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR9,000 crore, described as diversified and non-cancellable; management says there is no structural deterioration in demand.
Q4 and FY26 shortfall attributed to West Asia conflict, last-minute customer deferments, supply chain delays and product timing shifts; some revenue recognition shifted though orders remain valid.
Auto industry outlook cut from mid-double-digit growth (December projection) to single-digit or low double-digit, per management, which raised caution on offtake.
Aerospace, railway, defence, space and EV are being added to reduce dependence on any one vertical.
OSAT and PCB output expected to be export-oriented at first; internal versus external consumption still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah: What is the sanctity of guidance given the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore targets versus about INR3,600 crore actual, and the OCF miss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said the INR4,500 crore target implied about 55% growth, and blamed a large EV two-wheeler customer dropping about 90% of volume plus government project delays. On OCF, it said standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore while the metering business drove the consolidated outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Nitin Arora: Why no guidance, and what will move the INR600 crore negative OCF to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it now commits to outgrowing the market at twice market growth rather than a number. It expects the INR600 crore negative to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations the key lever.

qa_highlights.question: Renu Baid Pugalia: Share of metering in revenue, growth ex-metering, rail ramp-up and government-offtake risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering is about 20-25% of revenue, but about 60% of that business was already EMS supply. EV grew about 28%. Kavach has initial approval and trial orders, with H1 approvals and H2 bulk orders expected; rail growth of 20-25% is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Amber Singhania: Metering subsidiary revenue, EBITDA and receivables; why receivables rose despite the securitisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering revenue was INR971 crore and receivables about INR1,365 crore. Securitisation has only started with one bank, with about INR40 crore discounted in each of two quarters, because the bank needs first-month billing and collections; installation delays are the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Dhaval Somaiya: Pending meter count, and breakup of the other roughly INR740 crore of subsidiary revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending supply to be completed in 2-3 months, with a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension. Of the EMS revenue of INR2,655 crore, two foreign entities contributed about INR300 crore on average, and KEMPL is the main EMS subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Sumant Kumar: Why did intangibles rise by about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics capitalised about INR320 crore of intangibles. Amortisation was booked once in Q4 (about INR32 crore), and will now be booked quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: Do the INR1,000 crore OSAT and INR500 crore PCB production targets still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Kunhikannan said no such guidance was given. He estimated FY27 PCB output at INR300-400 crore and OSAT at INR250-300 crore, both export-led.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash flow: metering receivables of about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current; securitisation has discounted only about INR80 crore cumulatively.
Guidance credibility: the company missed its INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue targets, and the CFO was unavailable for the call due to health reasons.
Top management restructuring and role realignment flagged during the quarter.
Customer concentration: a large EV two-wheeler customer fell about 90%.
Government payment and installation dependency for smart metering; DISCOM and GENCO timelines.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles now recurs (about INR32 crore per quarter), which will depress PAT.
Auto industry outlook downgraded; OSAT and PCB ramp and internal versus external sales mix still undecided.
summary.management_tone: Defensive and apologetic on the guidance miss and cash flow, while confident on the EMS business, OSAT and PCB growth. Management was evasive on specific FY27 revenue and cash targets, offering market-relative growth and quarterly updates instead.
key_quotes: We did an aggressive top line growth in the year based on the order book and we got the electrification of the vehicle.
As I said, it is not a denied order, it is a delayed order. We sincerely apologize for that this has happened.
We are committing for our growth based on what market can pull in.
Our order book continues to be stronger at INR9,000 crores plus.
I think the inflection point has stopped and will come into the reduction, and we will come back in 3 quarters with positive results on specifically this entity.

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 revenue guidance but targets growth at about 2x the EMS market (15-18%), backed by OSAT Unit 2 (Q2 FY27), PCB and OSAT FY27 production estimates of INR300-400 cr and INR250-300 cr, a INR9,000 crore+ order book, and rail growth of 20-25%.
